The designed alloy ingots with a weight of 100 g for each were prepared by means of arc-melting in a Copper mold under an argon atmosphere. The purities of all raw elemental metals are beyond 99.95%. These ingots were remelted at least five times to ensure the chemical homogeneity.

Then they were sealed in vacuum quartz glass tubes and homogenized at 1573 K for 2 h in a muffle furnace. Finally, these solid-solutioned samples were aged at 873 K, 973 K, and 1073 K for 24 h, respectively. Each heat treatment was followed by water quenching.

In the solid-solutioned state, the matrix of Al2Ti6Zr2Nb3Ta3 alloy is dominated by the BCC solid solution, as presented in Fig. 3(a), from which the B2 nanoparticles might be precipitated because the weak (001) diffraction spots appear in the SAED pattern.
With the aging temperature increasing to 973 K, these BCC nanoparticles are coarsened obviously, in which the particle size and the volume fraction are r ∼ 30.0 nm and f ∼ 47.0%, respectively.
